item.title: Sendai Gyutan: Grilled Beef Tongue, Miyagi's Signature Dish — Guide
item.description: Grilled beef tongue (gyutan) is Sendai’s culinary trademark — thick slices of ox tongue, salted and aged, then char-grilled over binchotan charcoal until the edges crisp while the centre stays tender. The dish was invented after WWII by a Sendai restaurateur who didn’t want to waste tongue meat discarded by US military kitchens, and has since become the city’s signature, served in dozens of specialist restaurants around Sendai Station. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Sendai, Miyagi Hours Lunch & dinner, most restaurants Admission Set meals from ~¥1,500 Time needed About 1 hour Best time Year-round What to Try The classic gyutan teishoku (grilled tongue set with oxtail soup, barley rice, pickles).
